threads.body: The `@deprecated` tag points callers to `create()`, but `get()` returns `INSTANCE` (= `create(true)`), which still emits `process.command_args` / `process.command_line`. Migrating from `get()` to `create()` therefore silently drops the command-line attributes, since `create()` defaults to `create(false)`. Consider clarifying the Javadoc so callers who want the current behavior are pointed at `create(true)`, and those who want the new safer default understand the command attributes are omitted.

The lambda ignores its config parameter `p` and unconditionally calls `create()`, so command attributes are always suppressed in declarative config mode. This means the option declared in `metadata.yaml` (`declarative_name: java.resources.process_command_attributes/development.enabled`) has no effect — a user cannot opt back in via declarative config, which is inconsistent with the autoconfigure `ProcessResourceProvider` path. Consider reading the declarative property from `p` to drive `ProcessResource.create(emitCommandAttributes)`, or removing the `declarative_name` from `metadata.yaml` if it is intentionally unsupported.

replies.body: Removed the unsupported `declarative_name` from `instrumentation/resources/metadata.yaml` and added a comment explaining that declarative resource detection uses the separate process detector schema, which currently has no toggle for these attributes.
